subject: Impeachment of Cabinet secretaries
query: has a defense secretary ever been impeached
title: Has a defense secretary ever been impeached? What history shows
answer: No. No U.S. secretary of defense has ever been impeached. The closest case is William Belknap, President Ulysses S. Grant's secretary of war, whom the House impeached on March 2, 1876, minutes after he resigned. The only other Cabinet member ever impeached is Homeland Security Secretary Alejandro Mayorkas, in 2024.
body:
Belknap faced five articles of impeachment over a kickback scheme tied to a military trading post. According to the U.S. Senate, he resigned to Grant at the White House just minutes before the House voted unanimously to impeach him. At his Senate trial, a majority voted against him on all five articles, but none reached the two-thirds needed to convict, and he was acquitted on Aug. 1, 1876. Many senators who voted not guilty doubted the Senate had jurisdiction over a former official.

Mayorkas became the first sitting Cabinet secretary to be impeached when the House voted 214-213 on Feb. 13, 2024, over his handling of the southern border. On April 17, 2024, the Senate voted that both articles were unconstitutional, ending the trial without a verdict on the charges.

On Nov. 9, 2026, Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., filed a privileged resolution with eight articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, starting a two-legislative-day clock that requires House leaders to act by Wednesday, Nov. 11. Hegseth called them "sham articles of impeachment." Leaders could move to table the resolution, which would kill it without a vote on the charges. Impeachment needs a simple majority in the House; removal needs a two-thirds vote in the Senate.
in_the_news: Rep. Thomas Massie forced a House vote this week on eight articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.

faq.q: Has a Cabinet member ever been impeached?
faq.a: Yes, twice: Secretary of War William Belknap in 1876 and Homeland Security Secretary Alejandro Mayorkas in 2024. Neither was convicted.

faq.q: Has a Cabinet secretary ever been removed from office by impeachment?
faq.a: No. Belknap was acquitted, and the Senate ended Mayorkas's trial by declaring both articles unconstitutional.

faq.q: Can a Cabinet secretary be impeached?
faq.a: Yes. The Constitution allows the impeachment of "all civil officers of the United States," which includes Cabinet members.

faq.q: How many votes does it take to impeach a Cabinet member?
faq.a: A simple majority of the House to impeach, and two-thirds of senators present to convict and remove.
